Annual Meetings

Afternoon Session - 2005 Meeting

Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger reveal why Berkshire doesn't sell businesses despite disappointing results and promise their successors will provide the "same wonderful lack of oversight" of Berkshire's subsidiaries. Buffett also warns investors not to bet against America and makes a moral distinction between buying a stock and buying an entire company.

Sat, Apr 30 2005 • 1:00 PM EDT
Key Chapters —
  1. 3. Buffett: Don't bet against America
  2. 5. Munger: "Terrible" and "gutless" behavior led to asbestos problem
  3. 6. Our successors will provide the "same wonderful lack of oversight"
  4. 9. Buffett (D) and Munger (R) both endorse Social Security
  5. 12. "I don't see gold as a store of value"
  6. 16. "Unwise" economic policies, but no "Armageddon"
  7. 17. Why Berkshire's board is better
  8. 21. Why we keep companies despite disappointing results
  9. 22. Moral distinction between buying a stock and a company
